2. That subprocess command is hardcoded to `-s workspace-write` and `approval_policy="never"` in [runner_process.py:35](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_process.py:35) and [runner_process.py:38](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_process.py:38).

Root cause was **not timeout**. It was a validator mismatch.

1. `triage` single-stage subprocesses were defaulting to JSON output validation, but Codex triage stages write plain text.  
This made successful runs look like failures (`exit 1` after `exit 0`).  
Fixed in [codex_runner.py:38](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/codex_runner.py:38) by defaulting triage stage validation to `_output_file_has_text`.

2. I also hardened success handling so it only fails on real output failure:  
grace polling + stdout/stderr fallback for custom validators in [\_runner_process_attempts.py:295](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/_runner_process_attempts.py:295), with config fields added in [\_runner_process_types.py:26](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/_runner_process_types.py:26).

3. Added regression tests:
- triage validator default/override in [test_triage_runner.py:420](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py:420)
- delayed output + stdout fallback recovery in [test_runner_internals.py:557](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/review/test_runner_internals.py:557)

> AGENT

You’re right to ask. It re-entered triage because of a guardrail, not because the queue was finished.

What happened in code:

1. `resolve fixed` is hard-gated by triage freshness in [`resolve/cmd.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/cmd.py:159).
2. I ran `desloppify plan triage --stage observe`, and that command auto-starts planning mode if triage stages aren’t present (injects `triage::*`) in [`stage_flow_commands.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_commands.py:67).
3. Once triage stages are in queue and partially confirmed, `is_triage_stale()` returns `True` until triage is completed in [`stale_policy.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_policy.py:148).
4. So later `plan resolve` got blocked by [`guardrails.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/guardrails.py:107), even though we were mid-queue.

Current live state confirms this:
- `triage::organize/enrich/sense-check/commit` are still in queue.
- `observe` + `reflect` are confirmed, but triage is not completed yet.
- That’s why it says `TRIAGE MODE (2/5)`.

Also: the message text “new review issue(s) not triaged” is a bit misleading here; this block can also happen just because triage is in-progress, not only because truly new issues appeared.

i < ONBOARDING_STEPS.length + 2; i += 1) {\n      act(() => {\n        result.current.handleNext();\n      });\n    }\n    expect(result.current.currentStep).toBe(ONBOARDING_STEPS.length);\n\n    act(() => {\n      result.current.handleBack();\n    });\n    expect(result.current.currentStep).toBe(ONBOARDING_STEPS.length - 1);\n  });\n\n  it('resets to step 1 when modal opens', () => {\n    const { result, rerender } = renderHook(({ isOpen }) => useOnboardingSteps(isOpen), {\n      initialProps: { isOpen: false },\n    });\n\n    act(() => {\n      result.current.handleNext();\n    });\n    expect(result.current.currentStep).toBe(2);\n\n    rerender({ isOpen: true });\n    expect(result.current.currentStep).toBe(1);\n  });\n\n  it('toggles shake state and clears it after timeout', () => {\n    vi.useFakeTimers();\n    const { result } = renderHook(() => useOnboardingSteps(true));\n\n    act(() => {\n      result.current.handleShake();\n    });\n    expect(result.current.isShaking).toBe(true);\n\n    act(() => {\n      vi.advanceTimersByTime(499);\n    });\n    expect(result.current.isShaking).toBe(true);\n\n    act(() => {\n      vi.advanceTimersByTime(1);\n    });\n    expect(result.current.isShaking).toBe(false);\n  });\n});\nEOF",

Yes, that other-agent fix is **necessary**, not redundant.

What they identified is correct:
- Unscored subjective placeholders should not stay permanently suppressed.
- Clearing skip entries for unscored IDs is the right behavior.
- Tracking `resurfaced` in `QueueSyncResult` is important so those mutations count as real changes and get persisted.

What was still missing (and I fixed):
- Guard against `queue_order ∩ skipped` overlap in **all** subjective sync paths, not just one.
- Under-target auto-cluster path could still re-append skipped subjective IDs and recreate the false failure.

`desloppify` is currently behaving per its code, but the UX is confusing.

Why no scan prompt:
1. `workflow::run-scan` is only injected when `plan_start_scores.strict` exists.  
   See [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py#L279).
2. Your plan has `plan_start_scores = {}` right now, so `next` shows nothing.
3. This is intentional in current tests: no run-scan when `plan_start_scores` is empty.  
   See [test_queue_count_consistency.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/test_queue_count_consistency.py#L446).
4. Scan preflight also treats empty `plan_start_scores` as “no active cycle”.  
   See [preflight.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/preflight.py#L61).

What’s also odd in your state:
- `plan.queue_order` still has 7 IDs, but they are all `auto_resolved`/`false_positive`, so actionable queue is 0.

So: should it show scan when queue is empty?  
- In current implementation: **no, not always**. Only during an active cycle (`plan_start_scores` present).  
- If you want it to always nudge scan on empty queue, that requires a behavior change.

> AGENT

The root is a state-machine bug, not a timeout.

`desloppify next` only shows the post-flight `workflow::run-scan` item if `plan_start_scores.strict` exists. That gate is hard-coded in [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py#L279). But scan reconciliation clears `plan_start_scores` as soon as the queue is considered drained, in [plan_reconcile.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py#L136). So the tool is using the same flag for two different meanings: “we have a frozen cycle baseline” and “we should show the end-of-cycle scan prompt.” Once that flag is empty, `next` falls through to “Nothing to do,” even though the intended next step is scan -> subjective review -> triage.

There is a second bug behind the missing subjective re-review. In your current state, [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json) still has 20 permanently skipped `subjective::*` IDs, while [state-typescript.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/state-typescript.json) still has 20 unscored subjective placeholders. Before the sync fix, unscored subjective IDs that were skipped were excluded from reinjection, so they stayed invisible forever. That bug explains why a scan would not have resurfaced them correctly before the fix.

So the short version is:

- Primary root cause: `next` incorrectly keys post-flight off `plan_start_scores` instead of actual “queue empty and no deferred items” state.
- Secondary root cause: skipped unscored subjective dimensions were allowed to suppress mandatory review work.
- Incidental noise: the 7 IDs still in `queue_order` are stale resolved metadata; they are not what blocks the prompt.

This behavior is currently enforced by test, so it is not just accidental runtime drift: [test_queue_count_consistency.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/test_queue_count_consistency.py#L446).

> DEVELOPER

So what's a good, deep solution here?

> AGENT

A good deep solution is to make post-flight a first-class lifecycle, not an accident of `plan_start_scores`.

Right now `desloppify` has two separate bugs that collapse into the same bad UX:

- `workflow::run-scan` is gated off `plan_start_scores` in [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py#L279), even though `plan_start_scores` is really score-baseline metadata, not lifecycle state.
- Unscored subjective placeholders can be suppressed by permanent skips, so after scan there may still be mandatory review work that never resurfaces in [sync_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_dimensions.py).

The deeper fix is this:

1. Separate lifecycle state from score state.
   Add an explicit plan field such as `workflow_state.phase` or `postflight_state`, with values like:
   - `objective_work`
   - `awaiting_scan`
   - `awaiting_subjective_review`
   - `awaiting_retriage`
   - `complete`

2. Compute that phase from authoritative facts, not from one reused flag.
   The inputs should be:
   - actionable objective queue count
   - temporary deferred count
   - whether a new scan has happened since queue drain
   - unscored subjective IDs
   - stale/under-target subjective IDs
   - triage staleness / new review issue snapshot

3. Make `next` a lifecycle renderer, not just a queue renderer.
   It should only print “Nothing to do” when all of these are false:
   - objective work exists
   - deferred disposition exists
   - awaiting post-flight scan
   - subjective review work exists
   - triage refresh exists

4. Keep `plan_start_scores` only for score reveal.
   It should answer “what was the baseline strict score for this cycle?”
   It should not answer “what phase am I in?”

5. Treat unscored subjective placeholders as mandatory until first review.
   A permanent skip should not be allowed to hide a never-reviewed `subjective::*` dimension. That fix belongs in [sync_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_dimensions.py) and is necessary.

6. Promote post-flight actions into the same workflow system as other synthetic items.
   `workflow::run-scan` should be a real workflow item derived from lifecycle state, not an ad hoc empty-queue fallback in [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py#L270).

The least invasive implementation is:

- Add `postflight_state.awaiting_scan` to the plan.
- Set it when the last actionable objective item disappears and there are no deferred items.
- Clear it when `scan_count` advances.
- Change `_empty_queue_fallback` to use `awaiting_scan`, not `plan_start_scores`.
- After scan reconcile, resurface unscored subjective IDs even if skipped, then let triage sync run from the resulting state.
- Only then allow `next` to show empty.

That gives you the behavior you actually want:

- queue clears -> `run-scan`
- scan completes -> subjective review items appear
- review completes / review issues change -> retriage appears
- only then -> “Nothing to do”

If you want, I can implement that in `Documents/desloppify` as a proper state-machine patch instead of another local workaround.

> DEVELOPER

Thnk about the root of the problem - I want scan -> subjective review -> triage to be consistently injected when we start AND when the queue is empty (maybe they're the same thing), what'sa  good fundamentl soltion?

> AGENT

A good fundamental solution is to treat “start” and “queue empty” as the same lifecycle boundary: `no actionable objective queue` and `no deferred items`. That boundary should begin a single refresh pipeline, and `next` should always surface the first incomplete stage of that pipeline.

Right now the tool does not do that. It splits lifecycle across ad hoc places:
- [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py#L279) decides whether to show `workflow::run-scan` by looking at `plan_start_scores`.
- [plan_reconcile.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py#L136) clears `plan_start_scores` when the queue is drained.
- [sync_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_dimensions.py) separately decides whether subjective work should exist.
That means lifecycle is inferred indirectly from score metadata and skip state, which is the root mistake.

The better design is:

1. Introduce an explicit refresh lifecycle.
   Use plan state such as `workflow.refresh_epoch` or `workflow.phase`.
   `plan_start_scores` stays only for score reveal, not control flow.

2. Define one authoritative pipeline for empty/start state.
   The ordered stages are:
   - `run-scan`
   - `subjective review`
   - `triage`
   - then either `objective queue` or `idle`

3. Make stage completion explicit.
   A refresh epoch should track facts like:
   - whether a scan has been completed for this epoch
   - whether required subjective dimensions for that scan are fully reviewed
   - whether triage has incorporated the current review snapshot

4. Compute `next` from first incomplete stage.
   Pseudocode:
   ```text
   if deferred exists:
       show deferred disposition
   elif objective queue exists:
       show objective queue
   else:
       begin/continue refresh epoch
       if epoch needs scan:
           show workflow::run-scan
       elif required subjective review exists:
           show subjective review items
       elif triage is stale:
           show triage
       else:
           show nothing
   ```

5. Make subjective review mandatory until first real score exists.
   Never allow permanently skipped unscored `subjective::*` placeholders to suppress the review stage. That was the second bug.

The key point is this: `next` should not ask “do I have `plan_start_scores`?” It should ask “what is the first unfinished refresh stage for the current empty-queue boundary?” That gives you the same behavior at initial startup and after clearing the queue, because they are the same state.

If you want, I can implement this as a proper refresh-epoch/state-machine patch in `Documents/desloppify` instead of another local conditional fix.

> AGENT

**Implemented**

I separated post-flight scan state from `plan_start_scores`.

The root problem was that `desloppify` was using `plan_start_scores` for two unrelated jobs:
- score freezing for objective work
- deciding whether `next` should surface the post-flight scan

That made the scan stage disappear as soon as `plan_start_scores` was empty, even when the real lifecycle should have been `scan -> subjective review -> triage`.

I fixed that by adding an explicit refresh marker in [schema.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py) and a small lifecycle helper in [refresh_lifecycle.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/refresh_lifecycle.py). `workflow::run-scan` in [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py) now depends on that marker, not on `plan_start_scores`, and deferred items block post-flight instead of coexisting with it. I also changed [plan_reconcile.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/scan/plan_reconcile.py) so `plan_start_scores` only seed when real objective work exists, while scans that complete the empty-boundary stage mark the new post-flight completion state instead. `next` now always carries plan state into queue building, even for an otherwise empty plan, via [queue_flow.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/next/queue_flow.py).

I cleared that post-flight completion marker when real queue work changes again in [living_plan.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/resolve/living_plan.py), [override_skip.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py), and [override_misc.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_misc.py), so the next empty queue re-enters the scan stage instead of falling through to idle.

**Verified**

Targeted suites passed:
- `91 passed`
- `140 passed`
- `94 passed`
- `11 passed`

I also validated this on the actual `reigh` state:

1. Before scan, `desloppify next` now shows `workflow::run-scan` instead of `Nothing to do`.
2. I ran a real `desloppify scan --path . --skip-slow` in `reigh`.
3. That scan resurfaced the 20 skipped/unscored subjective dimensions.
4. After the scan, `desloppify next` now shows the `auto/initial-review` cluster with `20` subjective dimensions.

So the broken handoff is fixed in practice: empty queue now leads into scan, and scan now hands off into subjective review again. The triage handoff after review import is covered by existing sync tests and still passes.

- [test_cmd_next.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/test_cmd_next.py)

It’s properly progressing.

Current state of the live run:
- `11/20` batches have produced raw outputs.
- Active now: `#12`, `#13`, `#14`
- Queued: `#15` to `#20`
- Recent completions: `#11` finished in `128s`; `#7` was just a slow outlier at `325s`, not a hang.

What is a real bug:
- There is still a **runner messaging/validation bug**.
- Batch `#3` was reported as `failed (1)` because the subprocess exited but the immediate validator treated the output artifact as “missing or invalid”.
- But the batch **did** write a raw payload file: `batch-3.raw.txt`.
- The end-of-run collector in `desloppify` is designed to recover exactly this case if the raw payload parses cleanly.

So the precise answer is:
- `run-batches` is **not stuck**
- the job is **making real progress**
- there is still a **misleading intermediate failure signal** in the runner

What to improve in `Documents/desloppify`:
1. Runner wording
   - Don’t print `failed` for this state.
   - Print something like `execution validation failed; pending raw-payload recovery`.

2. Docs for `review --run-batches`
   - Document the two phases:
     - subprocess execution
     - final collection/recovery/import
   - Right now the logs make it look like a hard failure when it may still reconcile to success.

3. Troubleshooting docs
   - Explain where to check:
     - `run.log`
     - `logs/batch-*.log`
     - `results/batch-*.raw.txt`
   - Explain that long batches of `2-5` minutes are normal.

4. Skill/doc versioning
   - The skill doc warning about outdated `v3` vs current `v4` should be cleaned up. That’s unnecessary noise during normal runs.

5. Eventually: code, not just docs
   - The cleaner fix is to change the runner state model so “execution failure” and “final unrecoverable failure” are separate statuses.

If you want, I’ll keep this run going to completion and then patch that runner status wording next.

Why:

- `desloppify plan triage --confirm-existing` rejected the plan because only auto-clusters exist.
- `desloppify plan triage --stage organize` also blocks for the same reason.
- So there was no valid triage subagent stage to launch yet; first I need to create the manual clusters that the tool requires.

> DEVELOPER

can you share why you were cofused here?

> AGENT

Yes.

I was confused for three concrete reasons:

1. I conflated three different states
- `desloppify` has:
  - auto-clustered issues
  - triage-stage inspection/reporting
  - triage-complete manual planning
- I initially treated “issues are already in clusters” as meaning triage could be confirmed.
- That was wrong. The tool only accepts **manual, non-auto clusters** as valid triage structure.

2. The CLI output is misleading
- `desloppify plan triage` printed `All 59/59 issues are in clusters.`
- That sounds like incorporation is done.
- But the actual gate later says:
  - `Cannot confirm existing: no clusters with issues exist.`
  - `Cannot organize: only auto-clusters exist.`
- So the tool reports “clustered” in one sense, then rejects them in the sense that matters for completion.

3. I treated an inspection command like a mutating workflow step
- Running `desloppify plan triage` without stage args mostly shows state and guidance.
- It does not by itself complete triage or write the required manual structure.
- I should have checked the stage gates earlier instead of assuming the readout implied progress.

There was also a second source of noise:
- the subjective rereview runner had both:
  - a misleading intermediate “failed” status for a recoverable output-validation case
  - one real malformed JSON batch at the end
- That made it harder to separate “workflow state bug” from “review runner bug”.

The actual root of my confusion:
- `desloppify` uses “cluster” to mean two different things:
  - auto-generated grouping for queue display
  - manually enriched planning units required by triage
- The command surface does not make that distinction clear enough.

What I should have done sooner:
- inspect the manual-cluster gate in:
  - [helpers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/helpers.py)
  - [_stage_validation.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py)
  - [stage_completion_commands.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_completion_commands.py)
- then go straight to creating manual clusters instead of trying `--confirm-existing`.

So the short version is:
- I was not confused about the repo findings.
- I was confused about the **workflow contract** in `desloppify`, because the UI says “clustered” while the completion logic only recognizes a stricter manual-cluster form.

> DEVELOPER

But why didn't you use the subagent approach, was it not obvious that you should?

> AGENT

Yes. In hindsight, I should have used the triage subagent path sooner.

Why I didn’t:
1. I optimized for state recovery first
- The review run had a real malformed batch and a misleading intermediate failure signal.
- I focused on getting the subjective rereview imported cleanly before adding another agent layer.

2. I misread `desloppify plan triage`
- I treated it like an active planning engine.
- In reality, until manual clusters exist, it is mostly a validator/instruction surface.
- I should have recognized earlier that the right next move was the staged runner, not more manual probing.

3. I over-weighted deterministic local edits
- Once I saw workflow ambiguity, I defaulted to local inspection because it is easier to control.
- That was the wrong bias here. The task was exactly the kind of structured analysis/planning that the triage subagent pipeline is for.

So: was it obvious?
- After the subjective rereview imported: yes, pretty much.
- I should have moved to the subagent triage flow earlier instead of manually poking the gates.

The non-handwavy answer is:
- I used subagents for the subjective review.
- I failed to switch to subagents for triage because I mis-scoped the problem as “debug the workflow state” instead of “run the triage workflow.”

If you want, I’ll correct that now and use the subagent-based triage path for the remaining planning work.

- `For desloppify, prefer the built-in agent workflow at every analysis/planning stage; use manual commands only for recovery, verification, or patching runner bugs.`

> AGENT

Yes.

There is a specific intended subagent path in `desloppify`, and we should have pushed it earlier.

The intended flows are:

- Subjective rereview:
  - `desloppify review --prepare`
  - `desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import`

- Triage after rereview/scan:
  - `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex`

That second command is the important one I should have switched to. It is not just “use subagents somehow”; it is a built-in staged runner for:
- `observe`
- `reflect`
- `organize`
- `enrich`
- `sense-check`

It also auto-starts triage if needed and is designed to resume stages.

So yes, the right push would have been something like:
- `After review import + follow-up scan, run: desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex`

If we wanted to be more precise after partial progress:
- `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex --only-stages organize,enrich,sense-check`

Why that matters:
- Plain `desloppify plan triage` is mostly an inspection/guidance surface.
- `--run-stages` is the actual subagent orchestration path.
- I should have treated that as the default, not as an optional fallback.

So the short answer is:
- Yes, there is a specific way they should run here.
- Yes, we should have pushed hard toward `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex` once the rereview import and scan were done.

> AGENT

Root cause:

- The codex staged runner was using the **same stage prompt contract** as the manual/Claude path.
- That prompt explicitly told the subagent:
  - it had the `desloppify` CLI
  - it should record its own work
  - it should mutate `plan.json`
- But the codex pipeline is built the opposite way:
  - subagent returns plain text only
  - orchestrator records the stage
  - orchestrator validates and confirms it

So the reflect subagent got contradictory instructions. `observe` succeeded because it uses a separate batch prompt that already says “do not run `desloppify` commands.” `reflect`/`organize` did not have that protection.

Secondary contributing factor:
- Once the reflect subagent went off-task and tried to run `desloppify`, it hit a local CLI/import problem in the workspace checkout.
- That made the derailment worse, but it is not the primary cause.
- Primary cause is: **wrong prompt mode for codex runner**.

What I changed in `Documents/desloppify`:

- Split triage prompts into two modes:
  - `self_record` for manual/Claude orchestration
  - `output_only` for codex pipeline
- Codex pipeline now builds prompts with `output_only`.
- Output-only prompts now explicitly say:
  - do not run any `desloppify` commands
  - do not debug/repair/reinstall the CLI
  - do not mutate `plan.json`
  - return plain-text report only
- Removed remaining command leakage from codex-only sense-check prompts.
- Removed leftover “Build it using the CLI” wording from output-only organize prompts.

Files changed:
- [stage_prompts_instruction_shared.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_instruction_shared.py)
- [stage_prompts_instruction_blocks.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_instruction_blocks.py)
- [stage_prompts.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts.py)
- [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py)
- [orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py)

Tests:
- [test_triage_runner.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py)
- [test_triage_stage_prompts_flow_direct.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_stage_prompts_flow_direct.py)

- `37 passed`
- Real `reigh` prompt generation now confirms:
  - no cluster-create CLI commands in codex organize prompt
  - no permanent-skip CLI commands
  - no “Build it using the CLI”
  - explicit “do not debug the CLI/environment”

services: TriageServices,\n@@\n     handler = _STAGE_HANDLERS.get(stage)\n     used_parallel = False\n     prompt_mode = handler.prompt_mode if handler is not None else \"output_only\"\n+\n+ \"red\",\n+            )\n+        )\n+        return \"failed\", {\n+            \"status\": \"failed\",\n+            \"elapsed_seconds\": elapsed,\n+            \"error\": preflight_reason,\n+        }\n \n     if handler and handler.run_parallel is not None:\n         parallel_ok, merged_report = handler.run_parallel(\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

No. It was not running correctly end-to-end.

What was actually happening:
- `observe` and `reflect` did run through the codex subagent path.
- `organize` was not reliably executing as requested.
- The immediate cause in the live `reigh` state is that the saved `reflect` blueprint is invalid, so `organize` should never have been launched.

Actual blocker in `reigh`:
- The current reflect report does not account for every open review issue exactly once.
- Live repro now reports:
  - missing: `8b4e817f`, `33811d5e`
  - duplicated: `1e392bc5`, `0995846e`
- That means the organize stage was being asked to mechanically execute a broken blueprint.

So the core problem was not “the subagent refused to work.”
It was:
1. `reflect` could save an internally inconsistent plan.
2. `organize` could still launch off that bad plan.
3. triage-time `plan skip --permanent` used the wrong attestation contract.
4. failed triage runs were returning exit `0`, which hid failure from automation.

I fixed those in `Documents/desloppify`:
- [override_skip.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/override_skip.py)
- [attestation.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/attestation.py)
- [_stage_validation.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py)
- [stage_flow_observe_reflect_organize.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_observe_reflect_organize.py)
- [stage_validation.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_validation.py)
- [orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py)

What changed:
- `reflect` now fails if its blueprint misses or duplicates issues.
- `organize` now preflights that reflect blueprint and blocks before launching codex if it is invalid.
- triage skips now require a triage-appropriate attestation (`reviewed` + `not gaming`), not a code-fix attestation.
- invalid skip commands now exit non-zero.
- failed codex triage runs now exit non-zero.

Verified:
- targeted tests: `75 passed`
- lint: clean

Live behavior now:
- `PYTHONPATH=/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify python -m desloppify.cli plan triage --run-stages --runner codex --only-stages organize --stage-timeout-seconds 30`
- now exits `1` immediately and prints the real reason instead of hanging/timing out.

So the answer is:
- I was using the subagent path, but the triage queue was not being run correctly because `desloppify` allowed an invalid reflect blueprint to reach organize and hid failures badly.
- That specific failure mode is now fixed.
- The next real step is to rerun `reflect` and generate a valid blueprint before `organize` can proceed.

> AGENT

Implemented in `Documents/desloppify`.

What changed:
- `confirm-existing` no longer leaves the stale old `strategy_summary` in place when `--strategy "same"` is used.
- It now writes an explicit reuse summary: the existing enriched cluster plan was reused, not rebuilt from the latest reflect blueprint.
- It also records reuse metadata for auditability:
  - `trigger = "confirm_existing"`
  - `last_completion_mode = "confirm_existing"`
  - `last_completion_note`
  - `last_triage.reused_existing_plan = true`
  - `last_triage.previous_strategy_summary` when the old summary was replaced
- The confirm-existing organize record now carries reuse markers too.
- The triage UI/help text now says `--confirm-existing` reuses the current enriched cluster plan rather than materializing a new reflect blueprint.
- Completion output now says that explicitly as well.

Files changed:
- [helpers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/helpers.py)
- [_stage_records.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_records.py)
- [stage_completion_commands.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_completion_commands.py)
- [display_layout.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/display_layout.py)

Tests updated:
- [test_triage_completion_cleanup.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_completion_cleanup.py)
- [test_triage_stage_records.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_stage_records.py)
- [test_triage_split_modules_direct.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_split_modules_direct.py)

Verification:
- `50 passed`
- `ruff check` passed on the touched files

One live-state caveat:
- I tried to re-run `confirm-existing` in `reigh` to rewrite its already-completed triage metadata, but the CLI correctly refused because there are no active triage stages anymore:
  - `No planning stages in the queue — nothing to confirm.`
- So the code is fixed in `Documents/desloppify`, but the already-completed `reigh` plan still has the old stored summary unless we deliberately reopen/recomplete triage.

Natural next steps:
1. Reopen and re-complete triage in `reigh` so its stored metadata uses the new confirm-existing behavior.
2. Leave `reigh` as-is and continue executing the queue with the fixed tool behavior for future cycles.

> DEVELOPER

What's the difference between the living plan vs. actionable queue?

> AGENT

`Living plan` is the full backlog structure.  
`Actionable queue` is what `desloppify` currently wants executed next.

In your current state:

- `83 planned`
  - all planned work items/clusters in the active plan
  - includes items not currently surfaced at the top of execution
  - can include work gated by ordering, dependencies, batching, or review flow

- `28 actionable queue`
  - the subset currently eligible/selected for execution
  - this is what `desloppify next` and the queue commands are driving

- `17 skipped`
  - items present in plan state but intentionally not actionable

So the practical distinction is:
- `living plan` = total plan inventory
- `actionable queue` = currently executable slice of that inventory

See [adding_new_tool.md](docs/structure_detail/adding_new_tool.md).\n@@\n ### Shots & Generations\n@@\n - Data access: `useShotImages(shotId)` → see [data_fetching.md](docs/structure_detail/data_fetching.md)\n+\n+### Shared vs Domain Ownership\n+- Put code in `/src/shared` only when it is a neutral primitive, contract, or infrastructure layer that can be used without importing feature-specific behavior.\n+- Keep product workflows, Supabase-backed repositories, and stateful feature orchestration in `/src/domains`, `/src/features`, or the owning `/src/tools/*` module.\n+- `src/shared/components/ui/` is reserved for low-level presentational primitives and wrappers; feature-aware controls such as AI prompt actions belong in a feature/shared-product folder, not the UI primitive root.\n+- Cross-surface contracts should live in neutral shared type files instead of importing from a concrete widget folder just to reach a type.\n*** End Patch\n"

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/docs/structure_detail/frontend_architecture.md\n@@\n ## Contexts\n@@\n ### Provider nesting order matters\n \n See `App.tsx` for the hierarchy. Providers that depend on others must be nested inside them (e.g., `ProjectContext` inside `AuthContext`).\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Ownership Boundaries\n+\n+- `shared/components/ui/` is for low-level presentational primitives and thin wrappers only. If a component depends on app contexts, feature hooks, or workflow-specific behavior, move it out of the UI primitive root.\n+- `shared` can host neutral contracts and infrastructure, but feature orchestration, repository logic, and Supabase-backed workflows should live in the owning `domains`, `features`, or `tools` module.\n+- When two areas need the same type, extract that type into a neutral shared contract file instead of importing from one concrete widget package into another.\n+- Prefer folder entrypoints (`index.ts`) for reusable shared component packages so callers import the package boundary instead of deep implementation files.\n \n ---\n*** End Patch\n"
}

I found the root cause of this triage failure. It’s not a timeout and not a bad verdict; it’s a prompt/validator contract mismatch inside `desloppify`.

Evidence from the live run:
- The observe prompt still tells subagents to emit legacy one-line entries:
  - `[hash] VERDICT — evidence`
- The observe validator now rejects entries unless each one has `files_read`
- Batch `3/5` followed the prompt exactly for `[7e33eab5]`, and the validator still failed it

So the tool is currently asking for one format and validating against a stricter one. I’m fixing that in `Documents/desloppify` now so reruns don’t keep failing on the same mismatch.

What I actually ran in the latest sequence:
- `desloppify next`

Why it may have looked like that:
- `desloppify next` always rewrites `.desloppify/query.json` and prints the cached subjective/review counts.
- It also prints lines like `query.json updated` and `Subjective: ...`, which can look like a fresh review/scan even though it is just rendering existing state.
- The tool also still has a plan-state bug: one `plan resolve` attempt temporarily renamed the real `.desloppify/` directory to `.desloppify.json.corrupted/`. I restored it. That was a persistence bug, not a rescan.

What actually happened:
- The last completed triage in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json) is from **2026-03-09 17:01:17+00:00**.
- After that, there was a full subjective rereview run at [run_summary.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/subagents/runs/20260309_190816/run_summary.json).
- That later rereview/import changed the open review issue set.
- We never completed a fresh triage against that newer review snapshot.

Why `desloppify` says “new issues”:
- It does not look at “did a scan just happen”.
- It compares current open review IDs to the last triaged ID set:
  - current open review IDs: `45`
  - last triaged IDs: `59`
  - overlap: `0`
- So to the guardrail, all `45` current review issues are “new since last triage”.

That logic is in:
- [stale_policy.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_policy.py)
- [sync_triage.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync_triage.py)

So the root cause is:
- not “I just rescanned”
- it’s “the review snapshot changed after the last completed triage, and the triage snapshot was never refreshed”

Short version:
- latest commands: no fresh scan
- new issues appeared because the earlier March 9 rereview regenerated the review issue set after triage
- `desloppify` is now correctly treating that as pending retriage, although the messaging makes it look like a fresh scan just happened
